newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-BURKE LIFTS NSW TO WIN OVER NORTHERN TRANSVAAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BURKE LIFTS NSW TO WIN OVER NORTHERN TRANSVAAL.

text.p: Wallaby fullback Michael Burke scored a personal haul of 33 points to give New South Wales a much-needed boost with a 43-29 win over South Africa's Northern Transvaal in a Super 12 rugby union match on Sunday.

The peerless fullback scored three of his side's five tries and kicked four penalty goals and three conversions to single-handedly keep alive New South Wales' hopes of qualifying for the tournament play-offs next month.
New South Wales had languished near the bottom of the standings after a disappointing start which saw them lose three of their first four matches.
Burke's effort saw them jump two places to eighth, one point behind New Zealand sides Wellington and Waikato. Northern Transvaal slipped back one place to 10th.
Burke was the leading point-scorer in last year's tournament and so far this season has contributed 94 points of his side's tally of 144 from their first five matches.
His tally was boosted through a profitable period of 19 minutes in the second half when he crossed for his three tries to end any hope of a Northern Transvaal resurgence.
New South Wales scored 12 points in five minutes just before halftime through tries by number eight Fili Finau and centre Graeme Bond to lead 24-7 at the break.
Northern Transvaal opened the scoring when hooker Henry Tromp incongruously finished off a long backline movement to surge over for a try.
The South Africans hit back after halftime with a try to flyhalf Graham Bouwer but then Burke put the result beyond doubt with his three tries as New South Wales surged to a 38-12 lead.
A tiring New South Wales defence let through three tries by Northern Transvaal, allowing the South Africans to pick up a bonus point for scoring more than four tries.

The win kept up a perfect record for Australian sides in the sixth round of the tournament. Unheralded Australian Capital Territory moved to the top of the tournament standings with a 50-23 win over Free State on Friday while the disappointing Queensland scored their first win with a 37-24 defeat of Otago.

New South Wales - Matthew Burke; Alistair Murdoch, Graeme Bond, Richard Tombs, David Campese; Scott Bowen, Sam Payne; Fili Finau, Stu Pinkerton, Michael Brial, Sam Domoni, Tim Gavin (captain), Andrew Blades, Mark Bell, Cameron Blades.

Northern Transvaal - Kosi Alberts; Andre Snyman, Danie van Schalkwyk, Kosie van Vuuren, Jacques Olivier; Graham Bouwer, Joost van der Westhuizen; Adriaan Richter, Ruben Kruger (captain), Nicky van der Walt, Krynauw Otto, Derick Grobbelaar, Marias Hurter, Henry Tromp, Lourens Campher.
